lens: Simulated Mizuguchi lens: synchrony and touch; analytical exercise, not the real person's opinions.

strengths.finding: Successful cube pulses share one estimated audible landing for vibration, glow and kick; reduced motion suppresses kick and stale or hidden callbacks are guarded.
strengths.basis: Code inspection; focused timing unit test passed. No subjective listening inference.

strengths.finding: The small cube is an explicit instrument with press-time dispatch, while a repeatable six-note theme, anticipatory bar guide and graduated forms provide a coherent rhythm vocabulary.
strengths.basis: Code and three chapter screenshots. Screenshots show consistent restrained composition and distinct chapter motifs.

issues.finding: Several world cue timers still use scheduled audio time without output-latency compensation: nearby objects, singers and queued touch visuals can light before estimated audible output. This is a code-level inconsistency with the cube's compensated landing; perceptual magnitude was not measured.
issues.next_action: Route these cue times through the same estimated-output timing reference, then verify object and singer cues at nonzero output latency.

issues.finding: An empty-space tap dispatches its pulse only on release, although judgement retains its press timestamp; a short press can therefore be judged accurately while its response arrives later. The cube's immediate path is limited to a 24px radius and fingerTouch=false. This is an intentional gesture tradeoff, not a demonstrated regression.
issues.next_action: Measure perceived responsiveness for cube presses versus ordinary empty-space taps on a phone; preserve movement/hold disambiguation while making the immediate instrument gesture discoverable.

issues.finding: Reported output latency is capped at 400ms, so synchrony compensation does not represent devices reporting greater delays. The focused test covers only 0–400ms.
issues.next_action: Add a greater-than-400ms timing case and document or revise the cap using device measurements.

inspected: src/audio.js (660 lines; synthesis, output chain, scheduler, cue timing, rhythm and track dispatch)
evidence.absent: src/pulse-output-timing.js was not present in permitted file discovery.

executed.result: PASS: emitted-note timing at 0–400ms, reset/background cancellation, reduced motion, shared audible clock and waiting state assertions.
Blocked before browser startup: local HTTP server socket creation raised PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted. No browser assertions executed.

limits: Sensation is null because no actual listening, physical touch, vibration, interactive play or device latency measurement occurred. It remains unobserved rather than inferred from tests.
Audio score is technical code assessment only; timbre, musical quality, loudness comfort and clipping were not auditioned.
Visual score is provisional from three static 390x844 chapter screenshots; no animation timing, onboarding or full journey observation.
Only the permitted sources and screenshots were inspected; no README, HANDOFF, PANEL, historical reports or prior scores were read.
No repository edits, full suites or sub-agents. Full CI passing was supplied context and did not raise subjective scores.
